chapter: Early jobs and Johnny Lee Long show
title: First job at Milneburg with Chris Kelly
summary: At almost fifteen he worked at a dry dock, then played Milneburg on Sundays with Prince Miller, Bubba Green and Chris Kelly's band.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Yeah. Can you tell us about your first jobs then when you did, or did you get a job very soon after you got your drums aside from the fish fry? I know that's your job too, in a way. Did you play with any band pretty soon?

Kids or anyone else? Well, when I was around about, oh, I was going into, I hadn't quite made my 15. I'm going into 15 years old. I was working down at Janky Dry Dock. And I was able to buy some more, you know what I mean? Other traps and accessories. Some traps to go with the drums, you see? And my first job was out at Millenburg.
Oh, yeah, out there at the lake. That's right.
Out there with Prince Miller, Bubba Green, and...
Let's see, Bubba Green, what did he play? I can't remember.
He was a clarinet player.
He played clarinet.
He played clarinet.
Some of the men, I don't remember. I never met him, so I just can't... The names aren't always familiar.

That's right. Well, he was from Ruppen-Carlton, too. He's a little old fellow now. Is he still living? Yeah, he's still living, they tell me. I haven't seen him in a long time. Does he play anymore? No, he doesn't play, I don't think.
Yeah, I guess that's why I never...
I haven't seen him in quite a while. And, well, Chris Kelly, it was Chris Kelly's band then. And we used to play out there on a Sunday. We used to ride this train going out there.
You used to call it Smokey Mary. I never got the state that everybody talks about. That's right.
We used to ride out there. They had different camps out there, you know.
Yeah, I've heard about them. They still had a few little things like that out there, like Mama Lou's and those kind that I saw. Yeah, that's right.

It used to be wonderful. I mean, people used to enjoy themselves so much out there. And the band would start playing maybe around about, say, 12 o'clock in the day. And you'd probably end up maybe around about 1 or 2 o'clock that Monday morning, you see.
Yeah.
So my daddy used to raise sand because I'd be out there too late. Yeah. He wanted me in at 9 o'clock at night.
It'd take a long time to get back up home then. That's right.
But I told him, I mean, playing music like that, where you couldn't be in at 9, see. So it was one of those things.
